current_focus.summary: What the first build keeps and shows: the review record, the owner's moderation page, and what the storefront may read.

decisions.choice: Their own plugin, DinkusKit Reviews, in its own repository. It hands each product two numbers, an average rating and a review count, and the storefront and agent catalog read those without knowing how reviews were collected.

history.choice: Their own plugin, DinkusKit Reviews, in its own repository. It hands each product two numbers, an average rating and a review count, and the storefront and agent catalog read those without knowing how reviews were collected.

decisions.question: Do product ratings and reviews live inside Commerce or in their own plugin?
decisions.rationale: Owner, 15 Nov 2026 00:19 UTC, replying to that recommendation: 'agreed instead of merging in 128 lets actually scaffold the dinkuskit/* repo'. An owner gets reviews without choosing a third-party app as on Shopify, and Commerce stays small.

decisions.choice: Buyers only. A buyer reviews through a one-time link in the email sent after their order ships; the link proves they bought that product, so no account is needed. There is no open 'write a review' form in the first version. If one is ever added, a review from it stays hidden until the reviewer confirms by email, and is never published before that.

decisions.question: Who may leave a review: buyers only, or anyone?
decisions.rationale: Owner answered 'lock it' on 22 Nov 2026 to the four recommended answers. Hands-on study of the three most used Shopify review apps on a sandbox store (Nov 2026) and docs/research/product-ratings.md support it. The leading apps accept reviews from an open form by default and two of the three publish them before checking the email address, which invites fake reviews.

decisions.choice: Published straight away, for every star rating alike, because only buyers can review. The owner can hide spam and abuse afterwards and reply. A store setting switches to approve-first, and then every review waits, whatever its stars. Stars are never used to decide what is held back.

history.choice: Published straight away, for every star rating alike, because only buyers can review. The owner can hide spam and abuse afterwards and reply. A store setting switches to approve-first, and then every review waits, whatever its stars. Stars are never used to decide what is held back.

decisions.question: Is a review published straight away or does it wait for approval?
decisions.rationale: Owner answered 'lock it' on 22 Nov 2026 to the four recommended answers. Hands-on study of the three most used Shopify review apps on a sandbox store (Nov 2026) and docs/research/product-ratings.md support it. All three apps publish by default. Holding back only low-star reviews, which one app allows, risks the US rule against suppressing reviews (16 CFR Part 465).

decisions.choice: Each store's own rating, carried on that store's offer. Ratings are never blended across stores. A rating filter in the catalog tests the offer's own rating and count. Sharing reviews between stores owned by the same business is left for later.

history.choice: Each store's own rating, carried on that store's offer. Ratings are never blended across stores. A rating filter in the catalog tests the offer's own rating and count. Sharing reviews between stores owned by the same business is left for later.

decisions.question: When several stores sell the same product, does the cross-store catalog show one blended rating or each store's own?
decisions.rationale: Owner answered 'lock it' on 22 Nov 2026 to the four recommended answers. Hands-on study of the three most used Shopify review apps on a sandbox store (Nov 2026) and docs/research/product-ratings.md support it. Shopify's catalog filters on each offer's own rating; the review apps keep ratings per store. A blended score would let one seller's reviews raise or sink another's, and inferred product matches would mix unrelated products.

decisions.choice: No. The first version is stars with optional words. Photos, and any reward for adding one, come later on the owner's word; a reward would be offered the same for every star rating and the review marked as rewarded.

history.choice: No. The first version is stars with optional words. Photos, and any reward for adding one, come later on the owner's word; a reward would be offered the same for every star rating and the review marked as rewarded.

decisions.question: Do reviews carry photos in the first version?
decisions.rationale: Owner answered 'lock it' on 22 Nov 2026 to the four recommended answers. Hands-on study of the three most used Shopify review apps on a sandbox store (Nov 2026) and docs/research/product-ratings.md support it. Photos need media upload and more bundle room; collection, moderation and the rating should be proven first.

decisions.choice: In the store's own EmDash database, in the Reviews plugin's own storage. Nothing about a review or its buyer is kept on a DinkusKit server.

history.choice: In the store's own EmDash database, in the Reviews plugin's own storage. Nothing about a review or its buyer is kept on a DinkusKit server.

decisions.question: Where are review records kept?
decisions.rationale: Owner answered 'yes' on 22 Nov 2026. It follows the organisation's plugin architecture decision of 21 Nov 2026: customer details live in the store and keep working when dinkuskit.com is down. EmDash's built-in comments have no star, order or owner-reply fields.

decisions.choice: 14 days after the order is marked shipped, by default. The owner can change the number of days in the plugin's settings.

history.choice: 14 days after the order is marked shipped, by default. The owner can change the number of days in the plugin's settings.

decisions.question: How long after an order ships is the buyer asked for a review?
decisions.rationale: Owner answered '14 days works for me' on 22 Nov 2026. The three most used Shopify review apps default to 14 days so the parcel has arrived and been used; WooCommerce and BigCommerce use 7.

decisions.choice: Yes. Two public, read-only GET routes: rating (one product's average and count) and list (its published reviews, newest first, 20 a page, with the owner's reply). They return only what a shopper sees on the product page: stars, words, the name the buyer chose, the date, the reply. Never the order, the buyer's email, or a held, hidden or spam review. Nothing can be written through them.

decisions.question: May the storefront, the store's catalog feed and agents read a product's rating and its published reviews from the plugin without signing in?
decisions.rationale: The owner approved on 22 Nov 2026. Published reviews are public on every big platform, and the routes return only what a shopper sees on the product page.

decisions.choice: Whole stars from 1 to 5 are required. Words are optional, up to 2,000 characters, with no title. The name shown is the buyer's first name and last initial from the order; the buyer can change it or choose 'Verified buyer'. One review per product per order, and the buyer cannot edit it afterwards in the first version.

history.choice: Whole stars from 1 to 5 are required. Words are optional, up to 2,000 characters, with no title. decisions.question: What does a buyer's review hold in the first version?
decisions.rationale: The owner approved on 22 Nov 2026. The record in this build follows it; the buyer's review form, which enforces it, is a later pull request.

decisions.choice: Reviews asks the courier for the topic order.shipped from dinkus-commerce, 50 at a time, through a private courier/inbox route that refuses every signed-in caller. From each item it keeps, in the store's own database: the order id, the shipped date, the buyer's email and name, and the products bought (id and name). Nothing else in the item is kept. An item id already kept is ignored, so a repeated delivery changes nothing, and a second shipment of one order is a new item. The Reviews page says when the courier last came by or that it is missing, and never shows the buyer's email or name.

decisions.question: What does Reviews take in and keep when the store's courier brings news that an order shipped?
decisions.rationale: The owner approved on 22 Nov 2026. Follows the plugin communication rule and the courier's door contract, both approved by the owner on 22 Nov 2026. These are the fewest fields that let Reviews ask the buyer and prove the purchase. Commerce's outbox for this topic is not built yet.

decisions.choice: The store's own email sender: Reviews hands the request email to EmDash's email service in the store, the same sender the store's other email uses. No DinkusKit mail service is involved, and the buyer's email never leaves the store except to that sender. If the store has no email sender set up, no request is sent and the Reviews page says so.

history.choice: The store's own email sender: Reviews hands the request email to EmDash's email service in the store, the same sender the store's other email uses. No DinkusKit mail service is involved, and the buyer's email never leaves the store except to that sender. If the store has no email sender set up, no request is sent and the Reviews page says so.

decisions.question: Who sends the email that asks a buyer for a review?
decisions.rationale: The owner approved on 22 Nov 2026. Keeps buyer details in the store, as the records decision requires, and the email comes from the store's own address as it does on the big platforms. Not built yet.
